approvalTitle: requirements.md: reading and writing the dependency graph through FBL
content:
# Requirements Document

## Introduction

The user's request, verbatim (2026-10-09):

> Create spec workflow MCP specifications. One specification for converting one of the standalone diagram tools to FBL and DISL. i.e. analyse the current implementation, define the DISL and FBL and then write the specification on the refactoring., also focus on finding issues and aspects where the DISL and FBL languages do not yet cover everything.

This is one of the fifteen specifications that reading gives (the series and the survey behind it are in `causal-loop-disl-fbl`, *Introduction*). It converts the **dependency graph** (`generic/dependencies`, `.dgr`, ADP's own YAML).

**The dependency graph is half converted, as the timeline is.** Its toolbox, context menus, property rows and findings are derived from a bundled DISL 0.3 definition today, and a parity transcript holds them. Its body is still read by `DependencyGraphParser` and written by `DependencyGraphWriter`, which shares `LineSplice` with the timeline, and its DISL model is built from the parser's reading. No FBL binding for `.dgr` exists anywhere, so this document drafts one. This specification is the FBL half only: the body read and written through that binding, and the parser and the writer gone from the product code.

**The module is a fork of the timeline with the dates taken out, so the timeline's findings were checked here one by one.** Five of them (the timeline's B1 and B4 to B7) are answered per finding in the table *The timeline's findings, checked here*, each with evidence from this module's own code. Two come out differently: the empty flow sequence is not a runtime gap, and this module has a second scalar problem the timeline has not, in its two numbers.

## What was measured

Read on 2026-10-09: the module at `develop` `9a646009`; its bundled definition (etalii.adp `8f52fc5d`) and companion document; the FBL specification (0.2 draft) and the DISL specification (0.3 draft) in etalii-adp/etalii.adp at `develop` `da64ff0`; and `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` here. Nothing was built or run.

| Thing | State |
| --- | --- |
| The module's backend | 3,326 lines of C# in 48 files. `DependencyGraphParser` (127 lines) reads with YamlDotNet; `DependencyGraphWriter` (230) writes through the shared `LineSplice`; `DependencyGraphDefinition` (267) and `DependencyGraphFindings` (163) each build a DISL model from the parser's reading. |
| The DISL definition | Bundled, DISL 0.3, 565 lines, with an `x-dependencies` wire-id block and three plugins. Its `persistence` says `format: "plugin:net.etalii.adp.generic.dgr"`, and that plugin is declared `required: true`. |
| The FBL binding | None. No `.fbl` for `.dgr` is in etalii.adp or here, the conformance corpus has no `.dgr` fixture, and `RealFiles/divergences.json` has no entry for this tool. |
| The parity transcript | Exists: `Parity/dependency-graph.transcript.json`, 26 documents (the 11 fixtures, the example and its shipped copy, and 13 inline documents of `DependencyGraphCorpus.cs`), with a scripted edit sequence per document, the hunks each step made, and whether undoing every step restored the text. |
| The real-file check of a binding | None, because there is no binding. The 13 `.dgr` files of this repository have never been read through FBL. |

**How each finding is known:** *recorded* is a line of the transcript, a sentence in the module's code or in `definition/dependency-graph.md`, which a test or a reviewer already holds; *measured* is a search whose command is in *Sources*; *read* is a reading of the code against the specification text or the library's code, not run. Requirement 1 turns every *read* finding into a fixture first.

## Findings

The three kinds are those of `causal-loop-disl-fbl`: a **definition defect** is repaired in the definition or the binding, a **runtime gap** in this repository's libraries, a **language gap** in etalii-adp/etalii.adp. A **module defect** is a fault of today's code that the conversion would repair by accident and must repair on purpose.

### The timeline's findings, checked here

| Timeline | Applies here? | Evidence from this module | Here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1, typed scalars | **Yes, and wider.** | `DependencyGraphParser.Scalar` returns `scalar.Value`, the text, for `id`, `label`, `from` and `to`. The library hands a slot `value.Typed` (`TreeFamily.Cel`) and builds an id with `NewText.Plain` of that typed value, so `id: 007` is the id `7`. The numbers `x` and `row` add a second half the timeline has not. | B1, B2 |
| B4, empty flow sequence | **As a gap of the specification text only.** | The new document is `dependencies: 1` and `elements: []` (`DependencyGraphDocumentFactory`). `YamlFamily.Insert` in the library has a branch for exactly this (its comment: "An empty flow sequence [...] becomes a block sequence"), and the hype cycle's template `trends: []` depends on it. The timeline document's sentence that the planner has no code for it searched `Planning/`; the code is in `Files/Yaml/`. | B6 |
| B5, what a changed value writes | **Yes.** | `SetLabel`, `SetX`, `SetRow` and `SetRelationLabel` all call `LineSplice.SetKey`, which replaces the whole line with the key and a newly quoted value. | B7 |
| B6, where a new key goes | **Yes, and in the common case.** | `SetKey` inserts a missing key at `range.Start + 1`. Labelling a dependency that has no label writes `label:` between `id` and `from`. | B8 |
| B7, the gap after a dash | **No gap in the runtime; one difference beside it.** | `InsertElement` and `InsertRelation` take `LineSplice.IndentOf`, which copies the gap of the **first** entry. The library's `YamlFamily.Item` derives the gap from the key column of the **previous** sibling, so `-   id:` is copied too. | B9 |

### A. The DISL definition

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | `persistence` names the plugin `net.etalii.adp.generic.dgr` with `encoding`, `newline`, `finalNewline`, `files`, `ordering` and `omitDefaults`. With the binding it becomes `format: "fbl"` with `binding` and a `typeMap`; DISL 11.2 forbids those six keys beside it and says such a specification needs no persistence plugin, so the plugin's entry goes as well. The definition changes in etalii.adp and is bundled again, so its recorded sha changes. | Definition defect | Read |
| A2 | The definition's `writtenEnd` function (plugin `net.etalii.adp.generic.dependencyEnds`) **stays**, unlike the timeline's A2 hoped for its own. `std.references` carries `detail.missingId`, so a dangling end's sentence could be DISL's. Two things still need the id as written: an end written empty or not written is reported by no rule today (`no-from` and `empty-to` of `inline/dangling-relation`), and DISL does not say whether such an end "names nothing"; and `from: ghost, to: ghost` is a self-dependency although no node holds `ghost`. `hostAttributes` are "not visible in CEL" (DISL 11.2), so the function is fed from the binding's host attributes by module code. | Language gap (DISL 4.9), recorded in `dependency-graph.md` section 3 | Recorded |
| A3 | The order of the findings stays code (`DependencyGraphFindings.Judge`), because `constraints.order` sorts by code and cannot interleave two. This specification does not change it. | Language gap, already recorded | Recorded |
| A4 | The module builds its DISL model twice: `DependencyGraphDefinition.Build` adds each element under its **written** id, empty and repeated ids included, and `DependencyGraphFindings.Build` builds a second one through a synthesised `FblModel` with ephemeral ids. Under `typeMap` there is one model, built by `DislModelBuilder` from the binding's reading, in which a second holder of an id has FBL's place id. Every lookup by wire id (`ElementOf`: the first node with it, else the first dependency) must then go through the stored id, as the hype cycle's `GhgDefinition` does. | Definition defect, with a known pattern | Read |
| A5 | `addRight`, `addBelow`, `addNodeHere` and the tool's `createTarget` and `createSource` are run by the DISL runtime today and then **matched by shape** onto a module command (`Related`, `NodeHere`: "does not add one node with a label, an x and a row"), because "no DISL change says how to make" a splice. With the binding the transaction's changes are planned as they are, and the shape checks go. | None: this is what the conversion removes | Read |

### B. The drafted FBL binding against the module's parser and writer

| # | Finding | Kind | Known |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| B1 | **An id, a label and an end are the text they were written with.** `id: 007`, `label: 1.0`, `label: true`, `from: 0x1F` and `label: ~` are that text to the module. FBL 4.1.4 presents a plain scalar typed by the YAML 1.2 core schema, and a slot cannot ask for the scalar as written: the ids become `7` and `31`, the labels a number, a boolean and null. `id: 7` and `id: 007` in one file become one id. The module's own stated reason for keeping its reader (`DependencyGraphDefinition`: a second reader "would be a copy to keep in agreement with nothing gained") is a different one, so this is not recorded here as it is in `TimelineDisl.cs`. | Language gap | Read |
| B2 | **A number that will not read is zero, silently.** `X` and `Row` parse the scalar's text with .NET's invariant rules and fall back to 0: `x: sideways`, `row: 1.5` and `x: "270"` in quotes (which reads 270) all draw a node and raise nothing. FBL 7.4 makes "a value that does not convert to the attribute's type" an unreadable entry: no node, and `std.unreadableEntry`. The two readings also disagree on `0x10` (16 to FBL, 0 here), `.inf` (infinity, 0) and `Infinity` or `NaN`, which the X row accepts and writes and FBL would read back as text. | Language gap, and a behaviour change to rule on (Q4) | Recorded for today's side (`inline/unreadable-values`: no finding, three nodes); read for FBL's |
| B3 | **A dependency whose end names no node** is kept, sent to the canvas with its ids as written, and reported as `dependencies.dangling-relation`. FBL 5.4 creates no relation. The hype cycle's pattern answers it: the binding reads the entry as an element with reference attributes and `typeMap` maps them to the ends. For A2 the binding also reads each end a second time as a read-only host attribute. | Definition defect, with a known pattern | Recorded (`inline/dangling-relation`) |
| B4 | **An id missing or written more than once** is read as written, to report it and to find the first holder. FBL gives a stored id to one holder. The hype cycle's `storedId` host attribute answers it. | Definition defect, with a known pattern | Recorded (`inline/missing-id`, `inline/duplicate-id`) |
| B5 | **Nodes are read before dependencies, whatever the file's order.** With `relations:` written above `elements:` and one id held by a dependency and a node, the node keeps the id and the dependency is reported, on line 3. FBL 4.1 says "Reading order is document order", so `std.duplicateId` would report the node instead. The module hands the runtime each declaration's place in its own reading as its line to get this. | Language gap, or module code that reorders, to settle in design | Recorded (`inline/relations-before-elements`; the remark on `DependencyGraphFindings.Build`) |
| B6 | **The first node of a new graph.** The writer opens `elements: []` (or `[ ]`) into a bare `elements:` and appends. The library does the same with a `replace-value` over the text after the colon, which FBL 4.3 and the splice catalogue of 6.1 do not describe: 4.3 says a flow collection's "only writable span is the whole collection", and `ensure-container` is for a container that is missing. The bytes differ in one case: a comment after `[]` is dropped by the writer's whole-line replacement and kept by the library. | Language gap in the text only; no runtime gap | Read; today's bytes recorded (`inline/new-document`) |
| B7 | **What a changed value writes.** `SetKey` replaces the line with `key: value`, quoted only where `LineSplice.Quote` thinks YAML needs it. Lost: a trailing comment, the author's quotes, an anchor on the value (after which every alias to it names nothing and the file no longer parses). Left behind: the continuation lines of a block scalar. FBL replaces the value's span in its own style. FBL also quotes a new label that would read as another type (`123`, `true`), which `Quote` writes plain; `dependency-graph.md` section 9 records that as a defect. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read; the plain `123` is recorded |
| B8 | **Where a new key goes.** A key the entry lacks is written directly after the entry's first line: a first label on a dependency lands between `id` and `from`. FBL writes it where `insert.keys` orders it, after `to`. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Recorded (the step `set cmt0conn dependencies.label` of `comments.dgr` is an insertion) |
| B9 | **Which entry a new one copies.** The writer copies indentation and dash gap from the first entry of the list, FBL from the previous sibling (6.3). They differ only in a list whose entries are indented differently. FBL 6.3 says keys "align with the column after `- `" and does not say the gap is copied, though the library copies it. | None, or a gap in the text, to settle by fixture | Read (`indentation.dgr` holds the uniform case) |
| B10 | **What a removal takes.** The writer removes the entry's own lines. FBL removes its line span, which 4.1.1 extends "upwards over its leading comments": the comment lines directly above it at its indentation go too (`# Between two nodes.` in `comments.dgr`). Clearing a dependency's label is the same for a comment above the `label` line. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read |
| B11 | **Which dependencies go with a node.** The writer removes every dependency whose `from` or `to` equals the node's written id. For the second holder of a repeated id that removes the dependencies of the first; for a node with no id it removes every dependency with an end not written. FBL's `cascade` follows what a reference resolves to. | Module defect (Q5) | Read |
| B12 | **Undo does not always restore the bytes.** A rename, a relabel and a move are undone by the same command with the previous value, written through `SetKey`, so what B7 loses stays lost. The transcript records "the original text is NOT back" for 11 of its 25 documents with edits. The hype cycle undoes through the host's shared restore command, which restores text. | Module defect, recorded (Q5) | Recorded (`undoAll`; `dependency-graph.md` section 9) |
| B13 | **A graph with no `elements` key.** Adding a node throws (`InsertionPointFor` returns -1 and the writer inserts there). FBL refuses with a sentence, or creates the key when `insert.create` says where. | Module defect, recorded (Q5) | Recorded (`inline/no-elements-key`: "throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException") |
| B14 | **A key on the dash line with a wide gap.** `LineSplice.FindKey` strips exactly `- ` before it compares, so in `-   label: A` the key is not found, `SetKey` adds a second `label:`, and the document has a duplicate key and no longer parses. The same search matches a nested key of the same name inside the entry before the entry's own. | Module defect (Q5) | Read |
| B15 | **Findings FBL would add.** A sequence entry that is not a mapping is passed over in silence today and is an unreadable entry to FBL. A mapping that repeats a key makes the document unparseable and read-only today (YamlDotNet refuses it) and is `fbl.duplicate-key`, a warning on an editable body, to FBL. `dependencies: 1` is never read, so a `header` in the binding would add `fbl.header-mismatch`. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q2) | Recorded (`inline/unreadable-values`; section 9 for the marker); read for the duplicate key |
| B16 | **Merge keys and flow-style entries.** FBL 4.3 reads a merge key for reading; the module's reading through YamlDotNet's representation model does not, so a `row` given through one is 0 here. A node written as a flow mapping on one line is read by the module (and broken by its first edit, which inserts a line after it); to FBL it is one value with no writable member. | To settle by fixture | Read |
| B17 | **How X is written.** The writer uses .NET's shortest invariant text, FBL 6.3 ECMAScript's. `0.00001` comes back as `1E-05` here and `0.00001` there; `1e21` as `1E+21` and `1e+21`. | Behaviour change to rule on (Q1) | Read; today's form recorded (the X row of `inline/far-and-fine-coordinates`) |

### C. Language gaps, as they would be reported to etalii-adp/etalii.adp

1. **FBL: a slot that reads a YAML scalar as written** (B1). The timeline's first gap, now with a second tool behind it and one more consequence: an id is changed, not only a label. This one blocks the conversion.
2. **FBL: a value that does not convert, read as the slot's default** (B2). FBL has `default` for an absent slot only. With gap 1 answered a module can read the text and convert it itself; a way to say it in the binding would remove that code.
3. **FBL: reading order other than document order** (B5), for a format whose lists may be written in either order and whose ids share one space.
4. **FBL: opening an empty flow collection** (B6). The library does it; the specification does not say that it may, with which splice, or what happens to a comment on the line.
5. **FBL: that a new sequence item copies its sibling's gap after the dash** (B9), which the library does and 6.3 does not state.
6. **DISL: the written value of an end that names nothing, and whether an end written empty names nothing** (A2).
7. **FBL and DISL: a relation with a dangling end, and an id held twice or not at all** (B3, B4). Both are answered only by reading a relation as an element and carrying a `storedId`. This is the third binding that needs the detour.

## Open questions

Each is put to the user as a selection; the **(default)** is what this document is written against.

| # | Question | Options | Criteria affected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 | When an edit changes one value, adds one key or removes one entry, what is written? | **(default) What FBL writes**: the value's own span in its own style, a new key where the binding orders it, a number in FBL's form, and an entry removed with the comments directly above it; the transcript's edit hunks are regenerated once and reviewed as a diff. · **What the writer writes today**: the transcript stays byte-identical, and FBL first needs a whole-line rewrite, a key placed after the first line, .NET's number form and a removal without leading comments, each a language change. · Other. | 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, 1.3 |
| Q2 | Findings FBL would add that the tool does not give today (an entry that is not a mapping, a repeated key, a missing header). | **(default) Switched off where the languages allow**: no `header`, the unreadable entry kept and not reported; the repeated key is the exception, because FBL reads such a body and cannot be told to refuse it, so it becomes a warning on an editable graph and is named in the transcript's diff. · **Adopted now**, each named in the transcript's diff. · Other. | 2.6 |
| Q3 | Finding B1 blocks the conversion until FBL answers it. What happens meanwhile? | **(default) Report the gap and wait**, together with the timeline, whose Q3 is the same question: the requirements stand and nothing is built on a workaround. · **Work around it**: the module keeps a small reader for the scalars FBL types, named as standing in for the gap. · **Narrow the format**: an id or a label that reads as a number, a boolean or null must be quoted. · Other. | 2.2 |
| Q4 | A coordinate or a row that does not read (finding B2). | **(default) As today**: it is 0, the node is drawn and nothing is reported. · **As FBL reads it**: the entry is unreadable, not drawn and reported. · **Zero, and reported**: the node is drawn and a new warning names the value, which is what the parser's own comment promises ("the rules say so"). · Other. | 2.3 |
| Q5 | The module defects the conversion would repair by accident (B11 to B14). | **(default) Repaired on purpose**, each with a guard seen to fail against today's code and each named in the transcript's diff: undo restores the bytes, a node is added to a graph with no `elements` key by creating the key, a removal takes the dependencies that resolve to the node, and a key on a dash line is found. · **Reproduced**: today's answers are kept where the languages can state them, and each defect is raised afterwards. · Other. | 3.4 to 3.6 |

## Alignment with Product Vision

The product direction (2026-09-26) is one definition per tool, interpreted by a core in each IDE. The dependency graph is the plainest tool ADP has (one node type, one relation type, two numbers), so whatever stops FBL from reading and writing it stops every hand-edited YAML format. It is also the second tool behind the timeline's blocking gap, which makes that gap a property of the language and not of one module.

## Requirements

### Requirement 1: Every finding has a fixture first

**User Story:** As the owner of the tool, I want each claimed difference shown before anything is changed.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the work starts THEN one document SHALL be added to the corpus for each finding marked Read (A4, B1, B2 for FBL's side, B6, B7, B9 to B11, B14, B16, B17), the transcript regenerated from today's unchanged code, and the diff of the checked-in file reviewed as showing only the new documents.
2. Each *read* finding SHALL then be shown by a test that reads or edits its document through the drafted binding and compares with the transcript, seen to fail for the reason the finding gives, or the finding SHALL be struck from this document with that test as the reason.
3. WHEN a later step changes the transcript THEN the change SHALL be one this document names (Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5), regenerated on purpose. Any other difference is a regression.
4. The 13 `.dgr` files of this repository SHALL be read through the binding by `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` and compared, ids per type, with `DependencyGraphParser`, and every disagreement SHALL be an entry of `RealFiles/divergences.json` or a repaired binding.

### Requirement 2: The body is read through the binding

**User Story:** As a user, I want every `.dgr` that opens today to open the same.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module SHALL own its binding, `backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.DependencyGraph/dependency-graph.fbl`, embedded in the backend project; the definition's `persistence` SHALL name it with a `typeMap`, its persistence plugin SHALL go (finding A1), and the definition SHALL be bundled again with `bundle-disl.sh`.
2. An id, a label and an end SHALL be read as the text they were written with (finding B1), by the construct FBL gains for it (Q3).
3. A coordinate or a row that does not read SHALL be read as Q4 rules.
4. There SHALL be one DISL model, built by `DislModelBuilder` from the binding's reading; `DependencyGraphDefinition.Build` and `DependencyGraphFindings.Build` SHALL leave the product code, and an element SHALL be found by its written id as today: the first node with it, else the first dependency (finding A4).
5. A dependency whose end names no node SHALL be kept, sent to the canvas with its ids as written, and reported as `dependencies.dangling-relation` once per end that names an id; an end written empty or not written SHALL be reported by no rule; `from` and `to` naming one id SHALL be `dependencies.self-dependency` whether or not a node holds it (findings A2, B3).
6. Every finding the tool gives SHALL keep its code, severity, sentence, location and place in the order, the first holder of an id being a node before a dependency whatever the file's order (findings A3, B4, B5); and no finding it does not give today SHALL appear, but as Q2 rules.
7. A body that is not YAML SHALL open empty and read-only with the one finding `dependencies.unparseable`, as today.
8. WHEN the answers are compared with the transcript THEN the menus, rows, findings and payloads of every document SHALL be byte-identical, but where a question above rules otherwise.

### Requirement 3: Every edit is written by splices

**User Story:** As a user editing a file I also edit by hand, I want an edit to change what I changed and nothing beside it.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every command of the module SHALL write through `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` as a model change; a DISL transaction's changes SHALL be planned as they are and not matched onto a module command (finding A5); no module code SHALL build a line of YAML, and the module SHALL no longer use `LineSplice`.
2. WHEN a value changes THEN only its span SHALL change, in its own style (Q1): a trailing comment, the author's quotes and an anchor SHALL survive, and a block scalar SHALL be replaced whole.
3. WHEN a key is added THEN it SHALL go where the binding's `keys` order puts it, and WHEN an entry is added THEN its indentation and the gap after its dash SHALL be those of the entry before it (Q1, finding B9).
4. The first node SHALL be addable to a new document, and to a graph with no `elements` key (Q5); the first dependency SHALL create the `relations:` key at the end of the document, as today.
5. Removing a node SHALL remove the dependencies that resolve to it (Q5), in one undo step, with the count the confirmation states known beforehand as today.
6. Undo SHALL restore the body byte for byte, through the host's shared restore command, a `relations:` key the edit created included (Q5); the transcript's `undoAll` SHALL read "the original text is back" for every document.
7. A document ADP did not change SHALL be written back byte-identical, for every document of the round-trip corpus, the pair of line-ending fixtures and the one without a final newline included.
8. Every refusal SHALL keep today's sentence, the "does not parse" sentence of each command that remains and "A node cannot depend on itself." included.

### Requirement 4: What stays code, and what goes

**User Story:** As a maintainer, I want what remains in the module to be what the languages cannot state.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `DependencyGraphParser`, `DependencyGraphWriter`, the two model builders and `RestoreDependencyGraphLinesCommand` SHALL leave the product code. What a test needs of them as an oracle SHALL live in the test project.
2. The module SHALL keep the order of the findings (finding A3), the `writtenEnd` function over the binding's host attributes (finding A2), the X row's written form, the element mapper and the viewport filter, the session and the document store.
3. WHEN the conversion is complete THEN `dependency-graph.md` in etalii.adp SHALL list every remaining module class beside the gap or the host concern that keeps it, and its section 1 SHALL describe the binding and no longer a plugin.

### Requirement 5: The library work this tool needs

**User Story:** As a maintainer of the shared libraries, I want each thing this tool needs added once, for every tool.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. `EtAlii.Adp.Specification.Fbl` SHALL implement what FBL gains for finding B1, and for B2 and B5 if FBL answers them, each proven by a library test seen to fail first and by a conformance fixture vendored from etalii.adp.
2. A defect of the library that a fixture of Requirement 1 shows SHALL be repaired in the library; a language gap SHALL NOT be repaired here.
3. No module name SHALL appear in a library change.

### Requirement 6: Gaps are recorded and reported, never tuned away

**User Story:** As the owner of FBL and DISL, I want every place they fall short reported with its evidence.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. Each language gap of section C, and any the implementation adds, SHALL be recorded in `dependency-graph.md` with the construct concerned, the fixture that shows it, and what would resolve it; its section 9 SHALL lose the entries Q5 repairs.
2. The binding SHALL be offered to etalii.adp as an example beside `timeline.fbl`, with a conformance fixture for the empty flow sequence (finding B6).
3. A gap SHALL NOT be closed by weakening a check, skipping a fixture, or changing a fixture that was written before the code.
4. The delivery report SHALL list every gap as a candidate change for etalii-adp/etalii.adp, and SHALL say that the timeline document's finding B4 is a gap of the text and not of the runtime.

### Requirement 7: Documentation and gates

**User Story:** As a reader of the repository, I want its pages to stay true.

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. The module's `client/readme.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/solution-structure.md` where a sentence becomes false, and the remarks of `LineSplice` that name this module as a user, SHALL be updated in the change that makes them so.
2. All four gates SHALL exit zero on every pull request of this specification, judged by captured exit codes, with a newly created worktree built before a green gate is trusted about the bundled definition.
3. WHEN the tasks document is written THEN every acceptance criterion here SHALL be claimed by a task, established by diffing the two sets, and two traces SHALL be read back to their artefacts.

## Non-Functional Requirements

### Code Architecture and Modularity

- The module ends as its definition, its binding and the code Requirement 4.2 names. The house rules of `src/.editorconfig` and the three rules the gates refuse apply. `LineSplice` stays in `EtAlii.Adp.Documents`: four other modules use it.

### Performance

- Opening, validating and editing the largest `.dgr` of the corpus SHALL not be perceptibly slower than today; a text read recently SHALL not be read again, as the hype cycle's body does.

### Reliability

- No file that opens today opens differently. An unchanged document is written back byte-identical. Undo restores bytes. Every test written for a finding is seen to fail against it first.

### Usability

- Every sentence a user reads today is read unchanged, unless this document names the change.

## Out of scope

- The toolbox, menus, rows and findings: they are derived already, and this specification changes none but as the questions rule.
- The client: it compiles its notation from the bundled definition already.
- Changing FBL or DISL. The gaps are reported, and a language change is etalii.adp's own specification; Q3 says what this work does until then.
- The order of the findings and the dependency curve, which stay as they are.
- The other tools of the series, the .NET dependency graph included.

## Appendix: the binding, as drafted

A draft against FBL 0.2; no binding for `.dgr` existed to compare with. A dependency is read as an element with reference attributes, every entry carries the id it was written with, and each end is read a second time as written (findings A2, B3, B4), as the hype cycle's binding does. Two things in it are **not FBL**: `"as": "text"` marks where the construct of finding B1 is needed, and `"unreadable": "default"` where that of finding B2 is.

```json
{
  "fbl": "0.2",
  "bindings": {
    "dgr": {
      "title": "Dependency graph",
      "claims": { "extensions": [".dgr"], "origins": ["generic/dependencies"] },
      "body": { "kind": "file", "family": "yaml" },
      "reader": "declared",
      "text": { "newline": "crlf", "indent": 2, "sequenceIndent": "indented", "finalNewline": true, "quote": "double" },
      "elements": [
        {
          "name": "node", "type": "Node", "at": "/elements/*", "when": "entry.all(k, true)",
          "id": { "from": { "key": "id" } },
          "attributes": {
            "storedId": { "key": "id", "as": "text", "readOnly": true },
            "label": { "key": "label", "as": "text", "default": "", "empty": "keep" },
            "x": { "key": "x", "default": 0, "number": "shortest", "unreadable": "default" },
            "row": { "key": "row", "default": 0, "unreadable": "default" }
          },
          "insert": { "place": "after-last", "container": "/elements", "create": { "at": { "before": "relations" } }, "keys": ["id", "label", "x", "row"] },
          "remove": { "cascade": ["dependency"] }
        },
        {
          "name": "dependency", "type": "Dependency", "at": "/relations/*", "when": "entry.all(k, true)",
          "id": { "from": { "key": "id" } },
          "attributes": {
            "storedId": { "key": "id", "as": "text", "readOnly": true },
            "from": { "key": "from", "as": "text", "reference": { "to": ["node"], "by": "storedId" } },
            "to": { "key": "to", "as": "text", "reference": { "to": ["node"], "by": "storedId" } },
            "writtenFrom": { "key": "from", "as": "text", "default": "", "readOnly": true },
            "writtenTo": { "key": "to", "as": "text", "default": "", "readOnly": true },
            "label": { "key": "label", "as": "text", "default": "", "empty": "remove" }
          },
          "insert": { "place": "after-last", "container": "/relations", "create": { "at": "end-of-document" }, "keys": ["id", "from", "to", "label"] },
          "remove": { "container": "keep" }
        },
        { "name": "node-not-a-mapping", "type": "Unreadable", "at": "/elements/*", "readOnly": "This entry is not a mapping, so it is kept as it is." },
        { "name": "dependency-not-a-mapping", "type": "Unreadable", "at": "/relations/*", "readOnly": "This entry is not a mapping, so it is kept as it is." }
      ],
      "registration": { "createOnFirstPlacement": false },
      "template": { "text": "dependencies: 1\r\nelements: []\r\n" }
    }
  }
}
```

It declares no `header`, so that a missing or different `dependencies:` raises no finding (Q2). The template is byte for byte what `DependencyGraphDocumentFactory` writes, so the two agree. `create` on the node rule is Q5's default; without it a graph with no `elements` key refuses the first node. Four things are the design's to close with fixtures: whether a second read-only slot on a key that a reference slot also binds is planned as one write; whether `when: "entry.all(k, true)"` passes a flow mapping (finding B16); whether a removed `relations:` key should follow its last entry (today it stays); and which `fbl` version the library expects, because the hype cycle's own binding declares `0.1` while using `typeMap`.

## Appendix: the definition's persistence, as drafted

The `x-dependencies` block exists and does not change. The plugin `net.etalii.adp.generic.dgr` leaves `plugins`; `net.etalii.adp.generic.dependencyEnds` stays.

```json
{
  "persistence": {
    "format": "fbl",
    "binding": "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/etalii-adp/etalii.adp.ide.standalone/develop/src/diagrams/dependency-graph/backend/EtAlii.Adp.Diagram.DependencyGraph/dependency-graph.fbl#dgr",
    "ids": { "strategy": "uuid-v4", "encoding": "base36", "stable": true },
    "view": { "store": [] },
    "collaboration": { "mode": "none" },
    "typeMap": {
      "Node": { "as": "Node", "hostAttributes": ["storedId"] },
      "Dependency": { "as": "DependsOn", "attributes": { "from": "source", "to": "target" }, "hostAttributes": ["storedId", "writtenFrom", "writtenTo"] },
      "Unreadable": { "as": "unreadable" }
    }
  }
}
```

With `std.references` and `std.endpoints` switched off as they are today, the rules `danglingSource`, `danglingTarget` and `selfDependency` keep their text. Whether `std.unreadableEntry` can be switched off for the two `Unreadable` rules, so that a sequence entry that is not a mapping stays silent (Q2), is to confirm in design; the hype cycle's definition gives it a code and a message and does not switch it off.
